about: Recording batch E3d of ADR 0012, CF: the catalogue cases of CF-2 to CF-15, with the contested CF-12 cases (Q-CF-14) and the contested FX-40 cases (Q-FX-17); CF-13/c is given as CF-V2/a, which it also records. Each case is recorded on the CE oracle by a run of the fixtures below, or deferred with a milestone and a reason. TestRecordingBatches enforces it.

deferred.reason: it reads the deployed flow back with wmill sync pull; the harness pushes and runs but has no pull read-back (OR-8 covers the push). The oracle workflow's generate-metadata already writes the materialized fields into flow.yaml before the push (CF-6/a's fixture)

a raw submission or a version whose dependency job failed: outside the reference configuration, where windmill-lite applies the deployed defaults (ADR 0001 sections 1 and 7, Q-CF-13); the harness runs deployed flows by path only
a raw parent submission (Q-CF-15): windmill-lite never runs raw submissions, so ADR 0001 section 6 needs no recording; the harness runs deployed flows by path only

parts.reason: the oracle workflow runs generate-metadata before the push and its drift gate requires the committed tree to be that output, which writes skip_failures: true and parallel: false; the recording shows the deployed default's behaviour, the reference configuration (ADR 0001 section 1)
as CF-6/a: generate-metadata writes parallel: true, and skip_failure: true, parallel: true and expr '' on every branch that lacks them, before the push
windmill-lite never runs raw submissions (ADR 0001 sections 1 and 6, Q-CF-15); the by-path half, the reference configuration, is recorded

parts.part: the pending-dependency and raw-submission comparison runs ([[-999,-998,-997]])
parts.reason: outside the reference configuration (ADR 0001 sections 1 and 6, Q-CF-15); the by-path run after a successful dependency job is recorded, with the outer body's job kind flownode in the provenance

a flow pins a script by the hash the server assigns at deploy time, and the harness pushes one fixed tree; the runs d-raw, d-raw-path and d-script record the same question, whether the iteration's path is in the key
